stem: A postoperative abdominal incision separates and internal organs protrude through the wound. Which action should the nurse take first?

options.A: Cover the exposed tissues with a sterile nonadherent or saline-moistened dressing and notify the surgeon immediately.
options.B: Cover the organs with a dry nonsterile dressing and reassess later in the shift.
options.C: Force the protruding organs back into the abdomen before notifying the surgical team.
options.D: Ambulate the client to reduce tension around the incision.

rationale: Postoperative evisceration is an urgent surgical complication. NCBI nursing guidance directs the nurse to notify the surgeon immediately, cover the open wound with a sterile nonadherent or saline dressing to protect the exposed tissues, reduce tension on the wound, limit movement, and keep the client NPO for possible intervention. A is correct.
educational_objective: Initiate immediate protective wound care and surgical notification for postoperative evisceration.
source_organization: National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI Bookshelf)
source_claim_supported: For postoperative evisceration, notify the surgeon immediately and cover the open wound/exposed tissues with a sterile nonadherent or saline dressing while reducing wound tension and preparing for possible intervention.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation — medical emergencies and postoperative complications

source_original.stem: A post-operative client reports a sudden "popping" sensation at the surgical incision, followed by increased drainage and visible separation of the wound edges, with abdominal organs protruding. The nurse's priority actions include:

options.A: Cover exposed organs with sterile saline-moistened dressings and notify the surgeon urgently
options.B: Cover exposed tissue with a dry nonsterile dressing and reassess at the end of the shift
options.C: Attempt to push protruding organs back into the abdomen before notifying the surgical team
options.D: Ambulate the client immediately so movement can reduce tension around the open incision

source_original.rationale: Wound evisceration is a surgical emergency. Priority actions include covering the wound and protruding organs with a sterile saline-soaked dressing (never attempting to push organs back in), positioning the client to reduce abdominal tension (often low Fowler's with knees bent), keeping the client NPO in anticipation of emergency surgery, and notifying the surgeon immediately.
source_original.source_detail: Emergency management: cover eviscerated organs with sterile saline-moistened dressings, reduce abdominal strain, keep NPO and notify surgical team; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Replaced the secondary American Nurse source with current NCBI nursing guidance, removed the extraneous 'popping' cue, and retained only directly supported priority actions; difficulty reduced to medium.
